 <!--[[File:James Demmel.jpg|thumb|220px|James Demmel]]-->
'''James Weldon Demmel Jr.''' (born October 19, 1955) is an American [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]], the ''Dr. Richard Carl Dehmel Distinguished Professor of Mathematics and Computer Science'' at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="lbl"/>

In 1999, Demmel was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions to numerical linear algebra and scientific computing.

==Biography==
Born in [[Pittsburgh]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://advance.lexis.com/api/document?collection=directories&id=urn:contentItem:5RJ1-V9M1-JBH8-6333-00000-00&context=1516831|title=James W. Demmel|work=The Complete Marquis Who's Who Biographies|access-date=November 20, 2019|year=2017|via=Nexis Uni |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Demmel did his [[undergraduate]] studies at the [[California Institute of Technology]], graduating in 1975 with a B.S. in [[mathematics]].<ref name="hpcwire"/><ref name="sfar"/> He earned his Ph.D. in [[computer science]] in 1983 from UC Berkeley, under the supervision of [[William Kahan]]; his dissertation was entitled ''A Numerical Analyst's Jordan Canonical Form''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=James Weldon Demmel|id=27477}}.</ref> After holding a faculty position at [[New York University]] for six years, he moved to Berkeley in 1990.<ref name="hpcwire"/><ref name="sfar"/>

==Academic works==
Demmel is known for his work on [[LAPACK]], a [[software library]] for [[numerical linear algebra]]<ref name="hpcwire"/><ref name="siam"/> and more generally for research in numerical algorithms combining mathematical rigor with high performance implementation.<ref name="lbl"/> Prometheus, a [[parallel computing|parallel]] [[multigrid]] [[finite element]] solver written by Demmel, Mark Adams, and Robert Taylor, won the Carl Benz Award at [[ACM/IEEE Supercomputing Conference|Supercomputing 1999]] and the [[Gordon Bell Prize]] for Adams and his coworkers at Supercomputing 2004.<ref>[http://www.sc-conference.org/sc2004/awards.html Supercomputing 2004 Awards] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090204090133/http://sc-conference.org/sc2004/awards.html |date=2009-02-04 }}, retrieved 2011-05-04.</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Demmel was elected as a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1999,<ref name="siam">[http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=742 NAE Elects New Members] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428011903/http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=742 |date=2018-04-28 }}, [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]], May 22, 1999.</ref> a fellow of the [[Association for Computing Machinery]] in 1999, a fellow of the [[IEEE]] in 2001, a fellow of [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] in 2009, and a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 2011.<ref name="lbl">{{cite web |author-first=Jon |author-last=Bashor |title=Berkeley's James Demmel Elected to National Academy of Sciences |publisher=[[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] |date=2011-05-03 |url=http://www.lbl.gov/cs/Archive/news050311.html |access-date=2011-06-06 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606054005/http://www.lbl.gov/cs/Archive/news050311.html |archive-date=2011-06-06}}</ref><ref>[http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=News_May_3_2011_member_election Members and Foreign Associates Elected] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110507232125/http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=News_May_3_2011_member_election |date=2011-05-07 }}, National Academy of Sciences, May 3, 2011.</ref> Demmel was one of two scientists honored in 1986 with the [[Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis]].<ref name="siam"/><ref>[http://users.comlab.ox.ac.uk/endre.suli/fox/ Past prizewinners] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110522115314/http://users.comlab.ox.ac.uk/endre.suli/fox/ |date=2011-05-22 }}, 13th Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis, June 22, 2007.</ref> In 1993, Demmel won the [[James H. Wilkinson|J.H. Wilkinson]] Prize in Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing,<ref name="lbl"/><ref name="siam"/> and in 2010, he was the winner of the IEEE's [[Sidney Fernbach Award]] "for computational science leadership in creating adaptive, innovative, high-performance linear algebra software".<ref name="hpcwire">[http://www.hpcwire.com/hpcwire/2010-09-30/uc_berkeley_professor_james_demmel_receives_2010_ieee_computer_society_sidney_fernbach_award.html UC Berkeley Professor James Demmel Receives 2010 IEEE Computer Society Sidney Fernbach Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604040724/http://www.hpcwire.com/hpcwire/2010-09-30/uc_berkeley_professor_james_demmel_receives_2010_ieee_computer_society_sidney_fernbach_award.html |date=2011-06-04 }}, HPCwire, September 30, 2010.</ref><ref name="sfar">[http://www.computer.org/portal/web/awards/James-W.-Demmel James W. Demmel, 2010 Sidney Fernbach Award Recipient] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130530223327/http://www.computer.org/portal/web/awards/James-W.-Demmel |date=2013-05-30 }}, IEEE Computer Society, retrieved 2011-05-04.</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref> He received the [[International Parallel and Distributed Processing Symposium#IEEE Computer Society Charles Babbage Award|IEEE Computer Society Charles Babbage Award]] in 2013.

==Personal life==
Demmel is married to [[Katherine Yelick]], who is also an [[ACM Fellow]] and professor of electrical engineering and computer science at UC Berkeley,<ref>{{citation|url=http://archive.dailycal.org/article/7706/faculty_couples_keep_love_alive_at_work|title=Faculty Couples Keep Love Alive at Work|journal=The Daily Californian|date=February 14, 2002|first=Patty|last=Wong|access-date=October 4, 2011|archive-date=July 1, 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120701174302/http://archive.dailycal.org/article/7706/faculty_couples_keep_love_alive_at_work|url-status=dead}}.</ref> and Associate Lab Director for Computing Sciences at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]].<ref>
